eyebrow: Incident Response, Threat Hunting & SOC Capstone · Chapter 2
subtitle: Lesson 5 · Preparation: Building an IR Plan

eyebrow: A document you open at 2 a.m.

steps.label: Scope & objectives
steps.sub: what counts as an incident, what the plan is trying to achieve

steps.label: Severity classification
steps.sub: SEV1-SEV4 criteria, decided in advance, not improvised

steps.label: Communication plan
steps.sub: who gets notified, in what order, within what time window

eyebrow: The rest of the core components
code:
Escalation paths
  -- thresholds for moving a decision up the chain

Tool / access inventory
  -- offline creds, out-of-band channels, if the network is down

Legal & regulatory notification requirements
  -- GDPR 72hr, state breach law, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SEC
caption: Six components, one plan -- each one answers a question the team can't afford to debate live.

steps.label: Severity
steps.sub: lateral movement + ransomware = SEV1, no debate needed

steps.label: Comms
steps.sub: IC woken immediately, CISO in 30 min, legal in 1 hour

steps.label: Access
steps.sub: offline credential vault, since AD itself may be compromised

eyebrow: Why it has to survive the outage
code:
Plan stored only on:
  - the intranet wiki        <- useless if network is down
  - the CISO's laptop        <- useless if the CISO is unreachable

Plan stored on:
  - printed binder, offline vault, out-of-band chat group
caption: A plan nobody can open during the incident isn't a plan -- it's a historical document.

subtitle: Pre-thought-out response sequences for ransomware, BEC, exfiltration, and insider threats.
